tagline: Ten slow miles of coffee country above Kona.
intro: Route 180 holds to the Kona slope at 1,400 to 1,500 feet for about ten miles, from the Palani Road junction south through Hōlualoa village to Honalo. It is still two lanes with gentle curves, through the Kona coffee belt, lined with trees that in old Hawaiʻi marked the line between the lands running down to the sea and the lands running up to the mountain.
It began as a footpath around the island. The name grew out of Kamehameha's law of the splintered paddle, and in its later form it promised safe passage to everyone on the trail.

moments.title: Hōlualoa
moments.text: When the old post office was moved nearer the center of the village, the truck could not finish crossing the road, and the building spent the night in the middle of it.

moments.title: Kona Telephone Company building
moments.text: Luther Aungst made Hōlualoa the headquarters of his Kona Telephone Company in the 1890s, and mules dragged the poles across lava flows for a line from Hilo to Kaʻū.

moments.title: Donkey Mill Art Center
moments.text: Kona coffee farmers formed a cooperative and built this mill in 1954, when falling prices made a living hard, and today it is an art center.
